bullets.title: FOMC holds 3.50-3.75% with historic 9-3 hawkish split; 30Y yield hits 2007 high
bullets.body: Fed held rates steady at 3.50%-3.75% in a 9-3 vote—Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan all dissented in favor of a 25bp hike, the first triple-dissent since 2016. Chair Warsh explicitly rejected 'pause' framing, said there is 'no soft inflation target,' and signaled forward guidance should be reserved for crisis periods only. The 30-year Treasury yield surged to 5.21%, its highest since 2007, and JPMorgan now forecasts a 25bp hike in December 2026.

bullets.title: MSFT blowout: Azure +43%, $90B revenue, $175B CY2026 capex confirmed; stock +8-10% AH
bullets.body: Microsoft Q4 EPS $4.74 (beat $4.25 est.), revenue $90.01B (beat $87.72B), Azure +43% YoY—fastest since early 2022—and Azure crossed $100B annually for the first time. CEO Nadella added 31 data centers this quarter, 88 YTD, and confirmed ~$175B CY2026 capex (down from $190B due to extended asset-life accounting, not reduced spend). CFO Hood guided Q1 Azure growth ~45% in constant currency with H1 FY27 expected to accelerate; FY27 guided double-digit revenue growth and positive FCF.

bullets.title: META misses EPS, guides Q3 below consensus; FCF collapses 91%, stock -10% AH
bullets.body: Meta Q2 EPS $6.18 missed $7.14 est. (weighed by $1.18B severance and $2.4B legal charges); revenue $60.8B beat $60.24B est. but Q3 revenue guided $61-64B vs. $63.17B consensus. FCF crashed 91% YoY to $784M—lowest since Q3 2022—as quarterly capex hit $30.1B (+82% YoY). FY2026 capex guidance raised to $130-145B (floor lifted from $125B). META has now traded red 10 consecutive days and is down ~34% from its all-time high.

bullets.title: ARM beats Q1 but Q2 guidance in-line; smartphone royalties to dip slightly
bullets.body: ARM Q1 revenue $1.29B beat $1.26B est., adjusted EPS $0.45 beat $0.40 est., and ACV hit $1.73B vs. $1.67B estimate. Q2 guidance midpoint $1.38B is in-line with estimates, but the company guides adjusted opex below consensus at ~$780M. An exec noted smartphone royalties will decline slightly to low-to-mid-teens next quarter; one fintwit account flagged that in 'the greatest CPU market of our lifetimes, ARM can't muster a raise to the $2B customer interest level.'

bullets.title: Samsung Q2 record profit; forecasts worsening semi supply shortage 2027-2028; 2nm wins double
bullets.body: Samsung Q2 chip division operating profit 89.2T won with 52.2% margin; foundry booked 2nm orders from major CSPs and expects 2nm project wins to more than double in 2026. Samsung guides H2 server demand strength but soft mobile/PC demand and limited mobile profitability. Crucially, Samsung forecasts the supply-demand gap will expand into 2027-2028 and is allocating 60-70% of total capacity to long-term agreements with minimum pricing provisions.

bullets.title: Semiconductor index down ~30% MTD; Nasdaq 100 in -11% correction from June record
bullets.body: The SOXX semiconductor gauge fell ~30% month-to-date and the Nasdaq 100 entered a -11% correction from its June record close, its worst July on record. The chip selloff is being attributed to hyperscaler CDS/debt anxiety, SK Hynix earnings, and China's DUV capabilities—not a fundamental change in AI hardware demand. Meanwhile 2/3 of S&P 500 stocks remain above their 50-day MAs and S&P 500 Equalweight (RSP) is up 1.4% MTD near all-time highs.

bullets.title: MSFT capex: $15B/quarter on chips; $329B in uncommenced leases; Goldman pitching $5.4B data-center debt
bullets.body: CFO Hood said roughly two-thirds of Microsoft's $41B quarterly capex goes toward short-lived assets (mostly CPUs/GPUs), implying ~$9B/month on chips. Separately, Microsoft's balance sheet showed $329.1B in leases not yet commenced as of June 30. Goldman Sachs is marketing $5.4B in debt tied to a Microsoft data center project, and Microsoft signed $130B in data-center leases per FT.

bullets.title: META Q2 call: Zuck flags industry-wide compute scarcity, hints at compute monetization; FCF concerns dominate
bullets.body: Zuckerberg said there is 'insufficient compute capacity to meet demand' across the tech industry and that META sees opportunity to eventually sell compute externally—though margins on intelligence products are 'significantly higher' than on raw compute. CFO Li declined to give 2027 capex guidance. Multiple fintwit accounts noted META cannot raise revenue guidance despite epic capex, FCF has been consumed by AI spend, and the stock has no catalyst for a pivot while debt issuance replaces buybacks.

bullets.title: AXTI secures LTAs with LITE ($87M) and COHR ($22.3M) for InP substrate capacity
bullets.body: Applied DNA Sciences (AXTI) entered a long-term InP substrate agreement with Lumentum (LITE), which paid a $43.5M reservation deposit (total $87M LTA). AXTI separately secured an LTA with Coherent (COHR) with a $22.3M reservation payment. Fintwit noted these as positive signals for the broader photonics supply chain given China InP substrate access improving.

bullets.title: HOOD Q2 blowout: EPS $0.62 vs $0.41E; prediction market revenue ($156M) surpasses equities ($129M)
bullets.body: Robinhood Q2 EPS $0.62 beat $0.41 estimate; revenue $1.31B beat $1.21B estimate. Prediction market revenue hit $156M in Q2, surpassing equity trading ($129M) and crypto ($100M), with 13.6B contracts traded. Gold subscribers reached 4.8M (+17% YoY), Gold Credit Card surpassed 1M users, and 7M Trump accounts opened with $1.5B in contributions. CEO Tenev guided Robinhood Social to general public rollout by end of Q3 and signaled future non-US listed stock trading capability.

bullets.title: South Korea KOSPI down 33% MTD—worst month on record; $38.7B retail leverage losses
bullets.body: The KOSPI has fallen more than 33% month-to-date, surpassing the October 1997 (-27%) and October 2008 (-23%) crises to become the worst monthly decline on record. Citi estimated retail investors lost $38.7B (₩56T) on leveraged products, with 360,000+ margin accounts force-liquidated (62% under age 35). Regulators are reportedly considering a short-selling ban. Korean VIX reached 180, while US VIX remained near 20.

bullets.title: Retail investors sold net $243M in single stocks—largest one-day outflow since COVID crash
bullets.body: Retail investors dumped a net $243M of single stocks in a single session, the largest one-day outflow since the COVID crash, per Vanda Research. Corporate insiders were also selling at the second-fastest pace in 20 years in the weeks leading up to the selloff. One analyst called this a potential capitulation signal within 'another day or so.'

bullets.title: TSMC Kumamoto recovering from earthquake; 1.4nm fab ahead of schedule for April 2027
bullets.body: TSMC's Kumamoto fab tripped safety systems after a 7.1-magnitude earthquake but structure, power, water and safety systems are normal; equipment recalibration is underway. Separately, TSMC's 1.4nm fab in central Taiwan is ahead of schedule with first-phase piling complete and targeted for April 2027 completion. US senators also issued a formal warning to Apple against purchasing memory chips from Chinese firms.

bullets.title: SpaceX plans 4GW compute buildout using Nvidia Rubin racks; NVDA CEO visits Oval Office
bullets.body: A FundaAI report noted SpaceX plans to build 4GW of compute capacity next year using Nvidia Rubin racks—a detail described as underappreciated by fintwit. Separately, Jensen Huang visited Trump in the Oval Office and Trump praised Nvidia's chips; Nvidia also confirmed it is an investor in Elon Musk's xAI.

bullets.title: EQIX raises FY Ebitda guidance; co-packaged optics moving from development to early production
bullets.body: Equinix raised FY adjusted Ebitda guidance to $5.21-5.27B from $5.17-5.25B and AFFO to $4.24-4.30B, with the midpoint above consensus. Separately, an analyst noted co-packaged optics is moving from development into early production ahead of schedule, with implications for AVGO, MRVL, and TSM in advanced packaging.

bullets.title: Situational Awareness hedge fund (Leopold Aschenbrenner) seeks fresh capital after AI rout
bullets.body: FT confirmed Situational Awareness LP (SALP), Leopold Aschenbrenner's $20B hedge fund, is in talks with existing investors and lenders to raise fresh capital after heavy losses in the AI/semi selloff. The fund was up net 439% YTD as of June 30 but used leverage to amplify returns and is exploring letting investors purchase assets directly. Fintwit noted BE and SNDK had sharp drawdowns in July.

bullets.title: MSFT RPO +7.1% QoQ; GOOGL GCP beat guidance by ~82% vs 75-78% expected; AlphaFold team disbanded
bullets.body: Microsoft's remaining performance obligations grew $45B QoQ (+7.1%), while Google's RPO grew $51.9B QoQ (+11.1%). GCP YoY growth in 2Q26 came in ~82%, well above the 75-78% guidance range—the largest positive surprise in the quarter. Separately, Google DeepMind disbanded its Nobel Prize-winning AlphaFold team.

bullets.title: Warsh's 'hawkish hold' press conference: bond market signals credibility; no forward guidance
bullets.body: Warsh said the 42-day intermeeting rise in real and nominal yields was a 'top-decile' move and reflected the Fed's reduced forward guidance—characterizing it as working as designed. He stated the bond market and dollar are 'broadly signaling FOMC owns the situation.' Multiple accounts noted Warsh's first two Fed days produced the worst S&P 500 declines among any new Fed chair since 1994 (both >1% losses). JPMorgan now forecasts a December 25bp hike.

bullets.title: MU defended as non-commodity at $707; AAOI near 1x fwd revenue; SNDK 7%+ intraday reversal
bullets.body: One fintwit analyst argued MU is not a commodity despite trading down to $707 post-earnings, noting 16-layer stacking requires sustained capex with high barriers to entry. AAOI was flagged as trading close to 1x annualized forward revenue, with one trader saying 'hard to see some names drop much lower.' SNDK swung 7%+ intraday—opening higher, selling off, recovering, then closing down 7.32%.

bullets.title: US-Iran military escalation: CENTCOM strikes IRGC targets; Brent crude surges 7%+
bullets.body: CENTCOM confirmed a large-scale strike operation against Iran following attempted attacks on US military personnel; reports also flagged US Army HIMARS firing ATACMS and PrSM at targets in Iran, attacks on CPC tankers in Hormuz, and tanker fires overnight. Brent crude surged 7.3% to $88-91/bbl. Goldman no longer expects ERCOT to reach critical tightness by 2030 but maintains a structural tightening view in PJM power markets.
